sample_unit: LLM outputs (153 pathology cases x 4 LLMs)

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy, errors and hallucinations of general-purpose multimodal LLMs on histopathology cases
links.effect: Strict diagnostic accuracy 48.9% overall (36.6% to 58.2% across LLMs); errors in 82.0% of outputs, hallucinations in 76.6%; 90.2% had at least one error or hallucination.
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy alone substantially underestimates the safety limitations of general-purpose LLMs in histopathology.

links.outcome: Prevalence of errors and hallucinations, including in correct diagnoses, that clinician verification would need to catch
links.effect: 79.9% of strictly correct diagnoses also contained at least one error or hallucination; every strictly incorrect diagnosis contained an error and/or hallucination.
links.quote: Every strictly incorrect diagnosis contained an error and/or hallucination, while 79.9% of strictly correct diagnoses also contained at least one.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating error and hallucination burden of generated content, not just diagnostic accuracy, in pathology AI

screen.reason: Retrospective evaluation by 21 pathologists assessing diagnostic accuracy, errors, and hallucinations of four general-purpose multimodal LLMs on histopathology cases, without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
